_meta.purpose: Front-end/design INTENT registry for sidecoach-keyword.sh. The verb/mode registries fire on explicit sidecoach vocabulary (polish, forge, ...). This third tier fires on NATURAL front-end/design requests that contain no sidecoach verb, injecting an ACTIONABLE route directive that names the concrete first step (BUILD -> load the skill and run the matching flow; DIAGNOSE -> run /sidecoach audit <target> first) rather than a soft 'would it help?' self-question. It cannot invoke the skill for the model (a hook can only inject context), so this is the strongest self-start signal available: the model must still make the call. The goal is to ingrain sidecoach into the default evaluation of front-end work without bogging down trivial edits.
_meta.fire_rule: After no verb/mode match and outside the cooldown window, the intent nudge fires when ((a strong build/design ACTION or a DIAGNOSE signal) co-occurs with a SUBSTANTIVE_TARGET) OR (any STANDALONE signal appears). The DIAGNOSE tier exists because pure read-only diagnosis ('what's wrong with the homepage', 'diagnose the dashboard', 'take a look at the pricing page') is the canonical /sidecoach audit case yet carries no BUILD action - without it those prompts went silent even though the nudge text routes them to audit. Diagnosis verbs (review/inspect/check/look at...) are common in engineering prose, so the DIAGNOSE path uses its OWN positive allowlist DIAGNOSE_TARGETS of UI-dominant nouns - NOT the full SUBSTANTIVE_TARGETS. This is a safe-by-default allowlist (a newly-added overloaded target will not leak into diagnosis): it deliberately omits the cross-domain words that also mean HTTP/DB/SQL/data/code (header, table, view, grid, site='call site', interface='TS interface', component='sw component'), while keeping design-canonical targets (page, layout, section, screen, form, dashboard, hero, navbar, modal, ...). The BUILD-action path keeps the full SUBSTANTIVE_TARGETS list (its build verbs rarely precede those nouns). Informational framings (what is X / how to X / explain X / define X) are suppressed by the same logic the verb tier uses.
_meta.exempt_rule: A trivial-modify framing (EXEMPT) with no NEW_BUILD signal, no STANDALONE signal, and no DIAGNOSE signal stays silent - it is a tweak, not design work. A genuine diagnosis ('take a look ... and tidy it') is NOT silenced by an incidental tweak word. Minor targets (button, icon, color, font, label) are deliberately NOT in SUBSTANTIVE_TARGETS, so they never fire alone.
_meta.design_action_rule: DESIGN_ACTIONS (modernize/beautify/spruce up/facelift) are cosmetic verbs that overlap with backend nouns through the FULL substantive_targets list ('modernize the database TABLE', 'the TS INTERFACE'). They are held OUT of ACTIONS on purpose and fire ONLY when a DESIGN_ACTION_TARGET is present - a POSITIVE allowlist of design surfaces (page/screen/hero/button/component/card/layout/ui/... plus the design-canonical section/nav/form/modal/... targets). This is the whole gate: a design target present = fire; a backend object (api endpoint / graphql resolver / auth flow / cli parser / database table / typescript interface) is simply NOT in the allowlist, so there is no design target and no fire. NO prompt-wide backend blocklist is used - a blocklist is an arms race that over-suppresses legit UI prompts which merely mention a backend word ('modernize the settings PAGE and align it with the design system schema' must still fire, because its object is a PAGE). 'facelift' is target-gated like the others: 'give the button a facelift' fires (button is a design surface); 'give the API endpoint a facelift' stays silent (endpoint is not). The allowlist deliberately OMITS overloaded nouns (table/interface/view/grid/site/header) that also mean DB/TS/HTTP.
_meta.cooldown_rule: On ANY sidecoach engagement (verb route, mode route, or intent nudge) the hook touches config.cooldown_state_file. Intent nudges are suppressed while that file is younger than config.cooldown_seconds, so an active build and its follow-up tweaks are not re-nagged. Explicit verb/mode routes are NEVER suppressed by cooldown. Override seconds with env SIDECOACH_INTENT_COOLDOWN and the state-file path with env SIDECOACH_INTENT_COOLDOWN_FILE (used by the test harness).
_meta.pattern_syntax: Values are regex FRAGMENTS, matched case-insensitively with hyphen-aware word boundaries (?<![\w-]){pattern}(?![\w-]). Use [- ]? for optional space/hyphen and (?:a|b) for alternation. Tune freely - this file is the single source of truth for intent triggering.

nudge: This prompt reads as front-end / design work, so ROUTE it through sidecoach now rather than hand-coding or hand-eyeballing it. This is a route directive, not an optional 'would it help?' nudge: pick the branch that matches and take its FIRST concrete step. BUILD - if you are building or changing UI (a component, page, layout, hero, section, redesign, or a visual / type / motion pass), load the sidecoach skill and run the flow that matches BEFORE you write the markup; sidecoach owns strategy, tokens, typography, references, and motion, and its tilt-lab capability (the /tilt-lab skill) supplies any generative or shader background. DIAGNOSE - if you are being asked to look at, review, diagnose, or critique existing UI (for example 'what's wrong with this page', 'this feels off', 'look at <url>', 'is the copy real or fluff'), that IS a sidecoach audit and it is sidecoach's primary read path, NOT 'upstream of' it: run /sidecoach audit <target> as the FIRST step, before forming or stating an opinion. It RENDERS the page and runs the detection engine (contrast, heading order, broken images, justified text, tiny-text, nested-cards, marketing-buzzword, anti-pattern bans) - the objective and taste defects a freeform eyeball read provably misses - so do NOT answer a design or diagnosis request by eyeballing it when the audit is available. A hook cannot invoke the skill for you, so YOU must make the call - but for substantive UI work the default is to route to sidecoach; skip it only for a genuinely trivial tweak (one-line CSS, a copy change, a single prop).
